title: Python Code Tracer
creator: Hank Ratzesberger & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Six pre-authored Python programs replayed forwards and backwards, showing the current line, every variable with its value and type, and console output, with a prediction prompt before each state change.

learningObjectives: Execute a Python program mentally by stepping through it line by line.
Predict the value and type of a variable before it is revealed.
Explain how loops and conditionals change the order of execution.
State why floating point values must not be compared with ==
prerequisites: Chapter 13: variables, data types, functions, conditionals and loops

keyQuestions: What is the value and type of this variable after the next line runs?
Why does nothing after an unhandled exception run?
Which branch of the ladder runs, and why are the later tests skipped?
commonMisconceptions: A string that looks like a number can be used in arithmetic.
The value stored in a variable is the value printed to the console.
Every branch of an if/elif ladder is tested.
assessmentOpportunities: Scores well in prediction mode across several programs.
Explains the difference between average in the variables panel and in the console.
Identifies the zero-start in range() as the cause of the off-by-one program's output.
